title: Perf canary gating for profile-pack default changes (regression detection + bisect inputs)
creator: Talia Benson
related_links: Repo: perf-canary PR #388 (Add canary checks comparing latency deltas when default profile changes; integrate with Slack notifications)
Repo: benchmark-lab PR #913 (Persist results with profile_version and git sha tags)
Runtime PRs: #24979 (feature flag rollout), #25037 (schema validation), #25014 (profile version in /health), #24935 (scheduler_queue_ms metric)
description:
Goal
- Add automated perf-canary gating to detect regressions when default hardware tuning profiles change (profile pack updates, kernel set changes, scheduler/batching defaults).
- Provide deterministic “bisect inputs” so we can rapidly attribute regressions to: profile_version/profile_id changes, kernel set changes, scheduler mode changes, or runtime git SHA.

Why
- Profile pack will change runtime behavior without always changing model code. We need a guardrail that blocks or escalates when defaults regress p95/p99 latency or error rates, especially under mixed workload buckets.
- On-call needs attribution signals (what changed, and how to bisect) without manual log spelunking.

Scope
- Perf-canary rules for Hosted canary cohort (and reusable for Dedicated opt-in cohorts).
- Compare benchmark-lab (offline) and live canary (online) signals, with explicit pass/fail thresholds and a “warn vs block” policy.
- Include automatic bisect dimensions/labels in results storage and Slack notifications.

Non-goals
- Full automated revert/rollback (that is handled by SRE rollout tooling); this ticket provides the gating + signals.
- Model-quality eval gating (handled separately by Applied ML). This is strictly performance + reliability.

Proposed gating signals (initial)
1) Latency deltas (per SKU + workload bucket)
- p50, p95, p99 end-to-end request latency
- p95 and p99 decode latency (if available) or per-stage breakdown (queue_ms + compute_ms)
- Gate on relative delta vs baseline (previous default profile_version) with min absolute floor to avoid noise.

2) Throughput deltas
- tokens/sec (aggregate and per-GPU), requests/sec
- GPU util (if available from benchmark-lab) as supporting evidence (not a hard gate initially).

3) Reliability and resource risk
- error rate (5xx / timeouts)
- OOM events
- kernel fallback rate (kernel_choice fallback counters)
- scheduler queueing (scheduler_queue_ms) and queue depth saturation
- KV cache fragmentation / compaction time counters (supporting evidence; likely warn-only initially).

Acceptance criteria
- When a PR changes default profile selection or profile pack contents, perf-canary runs a standard subset of the benchmark matrix (per SKU) and posts a single Slack summary with pass/fail + top deltas.
- Blocking thresholds are enforced in CI for runtime-1.22 default-profile changes (at minimum on H100 and L40S). B200 suite allowed-to-fail until Infra driver baseline is stable.
- Each perf-canary result artifact is tagged with:
  - runtime_git_sha
  - profile_pack_version (a.k.a. profile_version)
  - resolved_profile_id (per SKU)
  - kernel_set (or kernel_variant label) + kernel fallback rate
  - scheduler_mode / workload_bucket version (if applicable)
  - benchmark_matrix_id (or matrix revision)
- “Bisect inputs” are printed in the perf-canary summary and stored alongside results (so on-call can rerun a specific combination quickly).

Implementation notes
- Define a canonical “Perf Canary Context” struct used by:
  - benchmark-lab runner output
  - perf-canary comparator
  - Slack notification payload
- Comparator rules should be per-SKU and per-workload-bucket, with noise guards:
  - require N samples (or minimum run duration)
  - ignore tiny deltas below an absolute threshold
  - prefer median-of-runs for offline bench
- Classification policy:
  - BLOCK: p99 regression above threshold OR error/OOM above threshold
  - WARN: p95 regression above threshold OR elevated kernel fallback / queue_ms above threshold
  - INFO: small deltas, or improvements

Suggested initial thresholds (to be tuned with SRE)
- BLOCK if:
  - p99 end-to-end latency regresses > 10% AND > 15ms absolute on any required bucket (H100, L40S)
  - OR 5xx+timeout rate increases > 0.05% absolute during canary window
  - OR any OOMs in benchmark-lab runs
- WARN if:
  - p95 end-to-end latency regresses > 7% AND > 10ms absolute
  - OR kernel fallback rate > 1% for workloads that should be on the primary kernel path
  - OR scheduler_queue_ms p95 increases > 20% vs baseline

Open questions
- Baseline selection: previous default profile_version vs pinned “known-good” baseline for each runtime release train?
- How to handle improvements that trade p50 for p99 (or vice versa) across buckets? (Likely require p99 non-regression even if throughput improves.)
- Dedicated cohorts: do we gate per customer pool or a synthetic Dedicated staging pool?

Rollout plan
- Phase 1 (this ticket): CI gating for profile default changes + Slack summary.
- Phase 2: integrate with SRE rollout checklist so canary go/no-go references perf-canary artifact links.
- Phase 3: add automatic “rerun with last-known-good kernel_set” helper for quick bisect.
comments: 2026-01-24 (Sahana Iyer): Drafted gating policy doc in perf-canary PR #388. Starting with WARN-only for kernel fallback counters until we validate thresholds on noisy workloads.
2026-01-28 (Marcus Reed): Please ensure gating compares per workload bucket (short prefill/short decode vs long context) — we saw regressions only on mixed buckets in earlier scheduler tuning.

2026-02-02 (Allison Grant): For Slack payload, include a compact table: SKU / bucket / p95 delta / p99 delta / error delta / kernel fallback rate. Also add links to Grafana panels when available (warn if not).
2026-02-05 (Sean Gallagher): Blocking criteria needs a hard OOM block and a hard timeout block. Tail latency block should use both % and absolute ms to avoid false positives on fast buckets.
2026-02-08 (Rina Kobayashi): benchmark-lab runner now exports profile_version + git sha tags (from PR #913). We still need to plumb kernel_set and scheduler_mode into the result metadata.

2026-02-12 (Sahana Iyer): Added “Perf Canary Context” fields to perf-canary comparator and Slack message. Pending: kernel_set label (waiting on runtime metric naming finalization from ENG-4925/PR #24911).
2026-02-17 (Rafael Mendes): Please add a single-line ‘bisect command hint’ in Slack output (what params to rerun in benchmark-lab). Even if it’s pseudo-command initially, it helps on-call.

2026-02-20 (Sahana Iyer): Updated thresholds per SRE feedback: BLOCK on p99 >10% and >15ms for required buckets; WARN on p95 >7% and >10ms. Added OOM = immediate BLOCK. Marked B200 suite allowed-to-fail until driver baseline is stable.
